title: Multi-value --lora-path/--lora-scale produce a LIST that crashes when fed to scalar pipeline kwargs
detail: The CLI registers --lora-scale/--lora-path as repeated/multi flags (action=append-style), so args.lora_scale / args.lora_path arrive as a Python list. Several command modules pass this list straight into a scalar kwarg: profile hands args.lora_path to pipeline.generate(lora_path=...) (expects one path), faceswap wraps args.lora_scale into lora_scales=[lora_scale] producing a nested list [[...]], expansion assigns the whole list to scalar lora_scale, and workflow stuffs the list into RunConfig.lora_scale (a float dataclass field). All four are latent crashes that only fire when a user actually passes the flag along that code path — static checks miss them. Fix pattern: unwrap to a scalar at the boundary, or make the pipeline kwargs accept lists consistently. Found via effort:low review-only scan (4 of 13 findings).

title: A flag's required=True is NOT satisfied by its --alias when both share the same dest
detail: refine.py registers --input-image with required=True, then app/commands/_shared registers --input to the SAME dest (input_image). argparse only recognizes the original option string for the required check, so a caller using --input (the alias) is rejected as missing-required even though the value landed in the dest. Net effect: the --input alias is permanently unusable for refine. General rule: when aliasing an option via shared dest, set required=True on only ONE registration and never rely on an alias to satisfy a required flag. Found via effort:low review-only scan (2 of 13 findings, one scored high).

title: Frame-floor helpers that early-return on a mod predicate bypass the minimum-frames guarantee
detail: video-vbvr._adjust_frames returns frames=1 unchanged when (frames-1)%8==0 — the modulo predicate is satisfied by 1 (since 0%8==0), so the 9-frame minimum is silently bypassed for that input. Pattern: any floor/ceiling helper whose guard is a divisibility/mod check rather than a direct comparison (frames < MIN) can pass the boundary value straight through. Always express floors as explicit numeric comparisons, not as side-effects of a mod branch. Found via effort:low review-only scan (1 of 13, medium).

title: A ternary expression used as a bare statement discards its value — correctness depends on side-effect ordering
detail: video-relay uses `x if cond else y` as a standalone statement (not assigned). The ternary evaluates only one branch and throws the result away, so any code that relied on BOTH branches' side-effects (e.g. shutil.move ordering) is fragile. Linters rarely flag it because it is syntactically valid. Rewrite as an explicit if/else so the intended branch's side-effect is unambiguous. Found via effort:low review-only scan (1 of 13, low).

title: effort:low review-only scan surfaces genuine latent bugs with ~0 adversarial overturn
detail: Default cheap lane (lanes:[review,lint], fix.mode=review-only) reliably surfaces real latent bugs across runs. 2026-06-19 run: 13 findings, ALL 13 passed adversarial verification (0 overturned). 2026-06-20 run: 6 findings, adversarialUpheld=0 again (1 high + 3 medium + 2 low; correctness(1)+argparse-integrity(3)+error-handling(2)). Takeaway: the low-effort review lane has a consistently high signal rate (≈0 adversarial overturn across two independent runs, 19 findings total); run it routinely and only escalate to medium+fix when you want changes applied. Adversarial-verify on effort:low is near-ceremony here — consider skipping it to cut cost on routine scans.

title: Findings cluster in command modules at the argparse→pipeline boundary (image-*, video-*, refine)
detail: All findings live in app/commands/ modules where argparse args (lists, required flags, defaults) meet pipeline dataclasses (scalars, fixed kwargs) — the type-coercion/dest-collision/default-bleed seam. 2026-06-19: 13/13 findings in app/commands/* (correctness + argparse-integrity), none in app/pipelines, app/workflows, or app/lib. 2026-06-20: again 6/6 in app/commands/* (image-purify, image-review, video-relay, video-segment, animate). Review focus on app/commands/* yields the highest bug density for this codebase; the boundary between user-facing argparse and typed pipeline constructors is the dominant defect locus. Lint lane (pyflakes/check-model/self-test) stays clean on code quality (pyflakesRealCount=0, selftestOk=true both runs); checkModelOk=false is an infra/model-state signal, not a code defect.

title: A hardcoded pipeline kwarg (False/None) silently freezes a feature even if a flag exists upstream
detail: In video-relay (LTXVideoPipeline construction), temporal_upscale=False is passed as a literal — not sourced from any arg or default. The relay defaults table also pins temporal_upscale False, and no --temporal-upscale flag is registered on the relay parser, so the temporal-upscale code path is permanently unreachable from the relay subcommand even though the underlying pipeline and the non-relay generate path support it. General trap: any kwarg constructed as a bare literal in a command module decouples the feature from the CLI surface — the flag can exist (or be assumed to exist) while the behavior is frozen. Fix: thread the value from args (default it in the defaults table, register a flag), or delete the dead capability so the frozen-False is honest. Found via effort:low review-only scan (high).

title: A flag registered in multiple sub-actions with differing intended defaults bleeds the first registration's default (first-writer-wins)
detail: Image sub-actions each add their own --seed/--output via guarded _arg_registered checks, but the guard only prevents a *duplicate add* — it does NOT normalize the default to the caller's intent. image-purify registers --seed default=42 (SeedVR2 noise), but the canonical t2i seed default is 777; whichever sub-action's parser builds first wins, so a user can get seed=42 semantics instead of 777 when the shared args merge. Same class: image-review --output (unguarded add in add_review_args, semantic conflict with purify --output). Trap: a guard that dedupes registration is not a guard that reconciles defaults — when the same dest serves sub-actions with different default intents, set the default explicitly at the action boundary (default=None sentinel + resolve at runtime), never rely on registration order. Found via effort:low review-only scan (3 findings: purify seed medium, image-review --output medium).

title: Bare subprocess.run(...) without except FileNotFoundError / Timeout wraps a crash in an unhelpful traceback
detail: video-relay._extract_last_frame calls subprocess.run([ffmpeg,...]) with capture_output=True, timeout=60 but no try/except. If the ffmpeg binary is missing, Python raises FileNotFoundError deep in the subprocess call (not a clean 'ffmpeg not found' message); if it exceeds timeout it raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired. The code only checks result.returncode AFTER the call, so the exception type is never converted to a user-facing message. Pattern: any subprocess.run on a possibly-missing external binary (ffmpeg/ffprobe/CLI tool) must be wrapped — catch FileNotFoundError and emit a guided install hint, catch TimeoutExpired and degrade. The helper also has a fallback second subprocess.run with the same gap. Found via effort:low review-only scan (medium).

title: A handle released on the happy path (cap.release()) is leaked if any later line raises
detail: video-segment opens cv2.VideoCapture(input_path), reads metadata, then calls cap.release() — but only on the success path. Any exception between open and release (or in subsequent detect_scenes/scenes_to_timestamps calls that still reference the video) skips release(), leaking the file handle / leaving the file locked on the OS. General trap: try/finally (or a context manager) is mandatory for any OS handle (VideoCapture, file objects, db connections) — a happy-path release() is not resource safety. Prefer with/contextlib.closing so the release is exception-safe. Found via effort:low review-only scan (low).

title: A command module that fully implements the contract (PARSER_META/add_args/run) but is absent from COMMAND_NAMES is unreachable
detail: animate.py implements PARSER_META, add_args(parser), and run(args) — the full command module contract — yet 'animate' is NOT in cli.COMMAND_NAMES ([image, refine, upscale, caption, replay, video, import-lora, import-workflow, check-model, schema-defaults, schema]) nor in COMMAND_ALIASES. So build_parser never registers it, `run.py animate` is an unknown command, and the module is dead code that still type-checks as valid (no static analyzer flags it, because it is internally complete). Trap: a module can pass every quality gate while being structurally unreachable. Guard: assert the module's name appears in COMMAND_NAMES (a one-line integrity test), or delete the stub. The repo already has test_selftest_integrity.py for a parallel case (deleted-test references); a COMMAND_NAMES-membership assertion is the analog fix. Found via effort:low review-only scan (low).
